questions.stem: Who owns the control flow in a coding agent?
options: The model decides what happens next.
The program decides what happens next.
Both the model and the program share control.
The user always has the final say.

questions.stem: What is an agent according to the text?
options: An agent is a model using tools in a loop.
An agent is a simple program that runs once.
An agent is a tool that never loops.
An agent is a model that only reads text.
questions.source_quote: An agent is a model using tools in a loop.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the feedback loop in an agent?
options: The feedback loop is only for the model.
The feedback loop checks the model's output against the specification.
The feedback loop is the same as the tool loop.
The feedback loop is not necessary for agent functionality.

questions.stem: What is the harness in an agent?
options: The harness is the model itself.
The harness is the code that runs the model.
The harness is only used for testing.
The harness is a type of feedback loop.
questions.source_quote: The harness is everything that is not the model.

questions.stem: In an agent workflow, who determines the steps?
options: The workflow is determined by the model.
The workflow is determined by the user.
The workflow is determined by the harness.
The workflow is determined by the feedback loop.
questions.source_quote: The model proposes. The harness decides.
